response: Yes, pectins are involved in cold acclimation and de-acclimation of winter oil-seed rape plants. Pectins, a type of cell wall polysaccharide, play a role in the modification of cell walls during cold acclimation, which helps to increase the plant's freezing tolerance. Changes in pectin composition and structure are associated with the cold acclimation process, and alterations in pectin methylation and solubilization have been observed in response to cold stress. Additionally, de-acclimation, or the loss of cold hardiness, is also accompanied by changes in pectin composition, suggesting that pectins are involved in the regulation of cold acclimation and de-acclimation in winter oil-seed rape plants.
